entries.group: G-defensive-except: a defensive exception type in a catch-all around the probe classifier, for a case the depth bound and the classifiers' own re-error handling already prevent (cf. carried reproducer_contract[32], 'defensive element for a type no producer can raise')
entries.grounds: verify's only guarded call is :203 `cls = catalog.registry().observation_class(spec.probe_id, spec.probe_digest, spec)`; :204-210 catches (OverflowError, RecursionError) and returns `no_meaning` (UNVERIFIABLE). Dropping RecursionError changes behaviour only if registry.observation_class (protocol.py:259-261 -> the per-probe observation_class) raises RecursionError; otherwise the `if cls is None` path (:211-212) and the OverflowError arm (kept) decide everything. At this snapshot no reachable reproducer makes observation_class raise RecursionError: (1) the two regex-bearing classifiers now catch it internally — cli_invocation._compiles (:440-447) and file_artifact._compiles (:263-275) both `except (re.error, OverflowError, RecursionError): return False`, so a 2000-nested-group pattern yields class None, not an exception (test_v21_r5_probe_model_data.py:295-299,331-336 assert observation_class is None / verify is 'no meaning' via the cls-None path; the file's own docstring :318-322 says the classifier catching it is the current fix and verify's except 'stays as the review's own' backstop); (2) the only exception that still propagates out of a classifier is the within_s-of-400-digits OverflowError from window_of/math.isfinite (python_callable.py:108-111), which the mutant KEEPS (test_v21_r5_probe_model_data.py:366-372 pass on the mutant); (3) the reproducer handed to the classifier is depth-bounded to <=DEPTH_MAX-1 = 63 levels by reproducer_contract (:159), and that bound was chosen so the contract/probe walks fit the caller's stack (test_v21_r5_review_deep_input.py:153-167), so a recursive walk of a reachable reproducer does not reach the interpreter's recursion limit. Measured: re.compile('('*2000+'a'+')'*2000) raises RecursionError on this interpreter (3.14.7), but it is caught inside _compiles, so verify's except is never entered for it. The removed arm is thus an unreachable defense-in-depth backstop; its removal is observable only if a future classifier regresses to propagate RecursionError. kill_check: ran all 12 registered kill files against the mutant, every one PASS (SURVIVED), including test_v21_r5_probe_model_data (the 2000-nested-group and 400-digit cases).

entries.grounds: Proof from the code. _deeper_than (:113-129) returns True at :127 (unchanged by the mutant) and False at :129 (mutated to None). entries.group: G-bounded-drops-finding: a reader depends on bounded returning the whole finding with only the deep fields marked; the mutant returns ONLY the marked deep fields and drops everything else
entries.grounds: bounded (:132-139): when `deep` is non-empty (a non-'reproducer' field nested deeper than DEPTH_MAX-1 = 63 levels), the original returns {**finding, <each deep key>: _NESTED_TOO_DEEP} — the whole finding with those fields replaced; the mutant returns {<each deep key>: _NESTED_TOO_DEEP} ONLY, dropping id, severity, summary, the reproducer, the `blocking` flag and every other non-deep field. Reviewer.review consumes bounded's output directly: adapters.py:144 `found = [review_verify.bounded(f) for f in found]`, then per finding :149 fid = redacted(str(f.get('id'))), :151 _verify(f) (adapters.py:288-290: UNVERIFIABLE if f.get('reproducer') is not a dict), :152 anchor(f) (guarded by isinstance(f.get('reproducer'), dict)), :156 blocks(), :163 Finding(fid, confirmed or bool(f.get('blocking')), ...), :166 redacted(found) -> RUN.json. So for a finding that carries a valid shallow reproducer AND a deep non-reproducer field, the mutant drops the reproducer -> _verify returns UNVERIFIABLE and anchor returns None -> a finding that the probe would REFUTE (CONFIRMED) and the bundle would ANCHOR no longer blocks; id becomes 'None' and the finding's reproducer never reaches RUN.json/the artifact. This contradicts bounded's own contract (:132-137 'finding with every field but its reproducer ... written as the marker ... The reproducer is left as it was stated') and Reviewer.review's invariant (adapters.py:113-116 'a confirmed finding is never passed silently'). The existing kill file does NOT catch it: test_v21_r5_review_deep_input.py:233 reads only V.bounded(...)['summary'] (present in both worlds); :215-227 uses a finding with NO reproducer and blocking=False so the drop of reproducer/blocking is invisible and finding/summary/severity happen to survive. kill_check: baseline PASS and mutant PASS on the registered kill file (SURVIVED) — the gap is real.
entries.refutation: INPUT: a finding f = {'id':'F-1','severity':'high','summary':'...','reproducer': <a valid shallow R-9/3 reproducer the probe REFUTES and the bundle anchors>, 'extra': ...} with one non-reproducer field made deep, e.g. {**f, 'summary': nested('list', DEPTH_MAX + 1)}, under policy fix-loop at min_severity 'low'. READER: review_verify.bounded (direct), and through it Reviewer.review (adapters.py:144 -> :151 _verify reads f['reproducer'] -> :152 anchor -> :156 blocks -> :163 Finding.blocks); also adapters.py:166 redacted(found) -> RUN.json and :159-160 preserve -> the artifact. SKETCH (minimal unit, add to DeepFindingsAreRows / the bounded test in test_v21_r5_review_deep_input.py): `b = V.bounded({**f, 'summary': nested('list', V.DEPTH_MAX + 1)}); self.assertEqual(set(b), set(f)); self.assertEqual(b['reproducer'], f['reproducer']); self.assertEqual(b['id'], f['id'])` — the mutant returns {'summary': marker} only, so set(b) != set(f) and b['reproducer']/b['id'] raise KeyError. STRONGER e2e (shows the harm): review a single finding with a CONFIRMED+ANCHORED shallow reproducer and a deep summary; assert the row blocks (row.blocks True, stated['verification'] CONFIRMED, stated['anchor'] ANCHORED); the mutant yields a non-blocking UNVERIFIABLE row with fid 'None'.
